findings: English->Indic, full set (320 items per system): sarvam-translate:v1 has the highest chrF++, 51.8 [50.1-53.5]. Next are mayura:v1 49.8, gemini-3.8-flash 49.7, claude-haiku-5.5 47.8, gpt-5.4-mini 46.6 and sarvam-105b 45.6. sarvam-translate is best of these systems in 8 of 10 languages (Gemini wins Kannada, Haiku wins Malayalam).

Frontier models do not beat sarvam-translate into Indian languages. On the 30 sentence-language pairs where every system ran, sarvam-translate scores 53.5 against gemini-pro-latest 51.9, gemini-3.8-flash 51.9, gpt-5.5 51.0 and claude-sonnet-5.5 51.0, all with thinking on. The CIs (about +/-5 points at n=30) overlap, so the honest reading is 'no better', not 'worse'.

Indic->English ranks the other way round: gemini-3.8-flash 64.3 [62.5-66.2], claude-haiku-5.5 62.1, gpt-5.4-mini 60.4, sarvam-105b 57.8, mayura 54.6, sarvam-translate:v1 52.5. On the 30-pair frontier subset, claude-sonnet-5.5 scores 65.9, about level with gemini-3.8-flash at 62.8. sarvam-translate's errors into English change the meaning. Hindi 'fabric ... shrinkage, or scorch' became 'clothing ... could lead to hypothermia or even burns', and Tamil 'appeared in court with covered faces' became 'was present in the court in the dock'.

Cost differs by about 80x for similar volume. sarvam-105b translated all 640 items for about INR 1.4 in tokens (34.5k in, 15.3k out). sarvam-translate and mayura each cost about INR 115 at INR 20 per 10k input chars (57.8k chars). claude-haiku-5.5 cost US$0.029 for the same 640 items, as reported by OpenRouter.

mayura:v1 modern-colloquial mode produces Hinglish/Tanglish copy: 61% of output letters are Latin, e.g. 'Fabric ரொம்ப hot ஆகாம பாத்துக்கோங்க'. Against the formal reference it scores chrF++ 16 vs 49 for formal mode. That is a deliberate change of register, not an error, and suits chat or marketing copy rather than formal training material.

Dubbing intelligibility (26 sentences x 6 languages per TTS, three STT judges): bulbul:v3 and gemini-3.8-flash-tts are statistically tied, and gpt-4o-mini-tts is slightly behind. CER with saaras:v3 as judge: bulbul 1.8%, Gemini 1.9%, OpenAI 2.4%. With the vendor-neutral gpt-4o-transcribe as judge: Gemini 3.5%, bulbul 4.3%, OpenAI 5.0%, CIs overlapping. With Gemini as judge, counting its refusals as failures: Gemini 5.9%, OpenAI 6.7%, bulbul 7.3%. Without the refusals those three are 2.8%, 2.3% and 2.3%.

Judge bias is small and not consistent. The neutral OpenAI judge slightly favours Gemini TTS. Saaras slightly favours bulbul. The Gemini judge refused bulbul audio most often (8 refusals vs 5 for its own TTS), and once refusals are excluded it scores bulbul and OpenAI best. Every TTS stays under about 5% CER with every judge.

Bulbul is fastest to first audio. Streaming TTFB p50 is 357 ms for bulbul, 991 ms for gpt-4o-mini-tts and 1154 ms for Gemini TTS. The full clip arrives at p50 1.69 s, 2.06 s and 2.89 s respectively. In a 2-call spot check, Bulbul's non-streaming REST endpoint took 5.8-7.6 s for the same text, so use the stream endpoint.

TTS cost per 10k characters: bulbul:v3 INR 30 (list price). gpt-4o-mini-tts about US$0.23, estimated from audio minutes at about $0.015/min. Gemini TTS used about 19.4k audio output tokens; no Gemini price is assumed. All three TTS produced audio in all 10 languages tested.

The local 30B models trail the APIs on the 8-sentence subset. Into Indian languages, sarvam-30b-local scores 37.8 and qwen3-30b-local 36.0, against about 45-50 for the cloud systems. Into English they score 55.2 and 53.4, close to mayura. sarvam-30b-local returned the English source untranslated in 9 of 80 English->Indic items (e.g. 'Lions are the most social cats...' in bn, ta, kn, pa), and added an unrequested extra paragraph once. Qwen3 always produced the target script.
caveats: chrF++ uses a single human reference per sentence. A correct paraphrase loses points, so differences under about 2 points on the full set, or about 5 points on 30-item subsets, are noise (see CIs).
FLEURS/FLORES sentences are general prose (news, travel, science), not real product copy or training modules. Brand names, UI strings and domain glossaries were not tested.

Test-set sizes are small. Price-matched systems ran 32 sentences x 10 languages x 2 directions (320 items per direction); the size was capped by the Sarvam translate price. Frontier models (thinking on) ran only sentence ids 1669, 1672 and 1701 x 10 languages x 2 directions (30 pairs per direction). Local models ran the first 8 sentences, because the shared llama-server was saturated (p95 latency up to 99 s). Compare systems only within the subset metrics.

LLM systems got a plain one-line translation prompt with no glossary. Before scoring, every system's output is cut to its first paragraph, so an unrequested 'Explanation' section does not count against chrF; this mattered for one sarvam-30b-local reply. Sarvam-30B runs with thinking off by prefilling an empty think block.

Dubbing measures intelligibility only, not naturalness, prosody, voice/gender fit or pronunciation of English loanwords. Sentences containing digits were excluded (26 remained). Voices: bulbul one named voice per language, Gemini Kore, OpenAI alloy plus a one-line 'read in <language>' instruction.

Gemini-judge refusals count as failures (CER 1.0): 20 of 504 benign transcription requests were blocked with BlockedReason.OTHER (bulbul 8, OpenAI 7, Gemini 5). This inflates the Gemini-judge CERs, and the finding also gives the numbers without refusals. gpt-4o-transcribe rejected the language hints 'pa' and 'or' (HTTP 400), so those 18 clips were transcribed without a hint.
During the run, Sarvam credits ran out once and many calls hit the shared 429 rate limit. Failed calls were retried and none are scored.

Spend for this suite: Sarvam about INR 328 (translate 231, bulbul 46, saaras about 32, 105b 1.4). OpenAI tokens and audio are recorded in usage; the TTS and transcribe estimates come to about US$0.73, and the chat models used a few cents. OpenRouter cost about US$0.09 as reported.
verdict: For localising formal English content into Indian languages, use sarvam-translate:v1. It was the most accurate system into Indian languages in 8 of 10 languages, and on a small subset no frontier model (gemini-pro, gpt-5.5, claude-sonnet-5.5) did better. Its lead over mayura:v1 and gemini-3.8-flash is only about 2 chrF, and it costs about 80x more per item than prompting sarvam-105b, so high-volume, lower-stakes copy can go through 105b or a price-matched model. For Indian languages into English (customer feedback, regional documents), use gemini-3.8-flash or claude-haiku-5.5. They lead sarvam-translate by 10-12 chrF, and sarvam-translate makes meaning-changing errors in that direction. Use mayura's colloquial mode only when you want code-mixed copy. For dubbing, bulbul:v3, gemini-3.8-flash-tts and gpt-4o-mini-tts are all intelligible in all 10 languages, with bulbul and Gemini slightly ahead. Bulbul starts playback about 3x sooner (357 ms) and has a simple per-character rupee price, so it is the best default for interactive voice and a fine choice for batch voice-overs. The self-hosted 30B models are not ready for production translation into Indian languages.
